phrase.text: Every piece of data has a type that says which values it can hold and what can be done with it; PseudoLearn has five primitive types and every other type is built from them.

runs.text: Every piece of data has a type that says which values it can hold and what can be done with it; PseudoLearn has five primitive types and every other type is built from them.
How to write it

blocks.description: Five boxes. Integer with the value 42; Real with 3.14; Boolean with its two values, True and False; Character with a single letter L; and String with the letters of Lucía in five boxes numbered 0 to 4.

caption.text: The five primitive types. Two hold numbers, one a yes-or-no answer and two hold text: a single symbol or a row of symbols.

runs.text: How it works
A variable is declared with
, its name, the word
and its type. From that moment it only accepts values of that type, and its type does not change while the program runs.

blocks.title: Lucía's card

rows.text: A number with a decimal part
The answer to a yes-or-no question
A row of symbols, even an empty one

runs.text: Think of the type as the shape of a container: an egg box holds eggs and a bottle holds liquid. You cannot keep soup in the egg box even though both are "for keeping". The analogy stops working at one point: some values do move by themselves from one container to another, as long as nothing is lost.
An
is a number without a decimal part. Integer operations give the
exact
result as long as it fits in the range. Going outside the range does not wrap around silently: the program stops.
A
is a number with a decimal part. When written it always shows at least one decimal, so it can be told apart from an integer at a glance.

blocks.title: Reals show their point

runs.text: The second line surprises almost everyone. It is not an engine bug: that is how reals work on any computer. A
cannot hold just any number; it holds the nearest mark on a very fine ruler that still has gaps.

blocks.description: A horizontal ruler with separate marks. The literal 0.3 points at one mark; the result of 0.1 plus 0.2 points at the neighbouring mark, 0.30000000000000004.

caption.text: The ruler with gaps. 0.3 and 0.1 + 0.2 fall on neighbouring marks of the ruler, so they are not the same number.

has exactly two values,
and
. It is the type of every question:
is not a number, it is a
. It is not a number, it has no order and it does not turn into text by itself. When written it appears with the profile's word:
in Spanish and
in English.
and
A
is a single symbol: a letter, a digit, a sign, a space or an emoji. A
is a row of characters that may be empty. Positions inside a string count from zero.

The language only converts a value on its own when no information can be lost: from
to
and from
to
. Everything else is requested with a function, because how to convert is the decision of whoever writes the program.

runs.text: A number does not stick to a text with
; it has to be converted or separated with commas:

blocks.title: A number does not stick to a text

diagnostics.message: Cannot concatenate number with text; use conversion function or separate expressions with comma

runs.text: And a real does not fit into an integer on its own:

blocks.title: A real does not fit into an integer

diagnostics.message: Incompatible types in assignment: cannot assign real to integer

runs.text: Before running, the engine translates the program into its intermediate representation. Each constant says what kind of value it produces:
(64-bit integer),
(real),
and
. Since the type of every value is known when compiling, the virtual machine never asks "what are you?" at each step.
The four fixed-size types fit in one machine slot; a string can be any length, so it lives on the heap and the slot only holds a reference.

points.text: The type of a variable never changes.
is exact within its range; going outside stops the program.
holds the nearest mark on a finite ruler and always shows a decimal.
is not a number and has no order.
